messages:
sara: paging team — seeing a sudden spike of GPU OOMs on decode-streaming hosts (region-us-west-2). Multiple containers restarting, large number of request drops. customer errors spiking in dashboards. I’m triaging, paging oncall.
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT opened: decode-stream-gpu-ooms (severity: high). Pager: @sara oncall. Links: https://telemetry/redwood/incidents/4324567890 — automatic collection started.
meera: sending initial SOC update to CS: have list of affected customers?
cs-liaison: we have 3 customers reporting 503s: acme-corp, quickscribe, edu-ai. acme is in prod, high volume. Quickscribe is currently using streaming w/ unbounded max_tokens in some routes.
sara: confirmed. logs show runaway generation from a particular client routing to decode-rt-38/39. max_tokens header present but some SDKs sending 0 or very large. suspect client-side bug + missing server-side cap.
julian: can we apply a per-route max_tokens enforced override? we pushed a soft cap last month but looks like routing bypassed it for legacy endpoints.
kevin: oncall-ing in 5. will join in 2. suggestion: quarantine offending API key, enable short-circuit on model variant, and temporarily block streaming on legacy endpoints.
sara: steps i’m doing now: 1) identify offending API key(s) — running query on request logs, 2) apply temporary quota/ban for those keys, 3) scale up decode pool to buy time, 4) roll out emergency config to enforce max_tokens=512 for streaming routes.
meera: sample query: ```sql
SELECT api_key, count(*) AS errs FROM requests
WHERE path LIKE '%/v1/stream%' AND response_code >= 500
AND timestamp > now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY api_key
ORDER BY errs DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
sara: results: api_key=ak_live_17 showing 84% of recent failures and continuous long-decoding sessions. tagging as suspect.
ops-bot: action: executed scale-up: decode-cluster-usw2 +3 nodes (p3x2). ETA ~90s.
julian: config push to enforce per-request cap: use `redctl config set runtime.streaming.max_tokens_override 512 --target=us-west-2` — i can push canary to 10% of traffic first.
sara: go ahead canary 10% now, then 100% if stable. also start draining decode-rt-39 (highest OOM count) for investigation.
julian: canary applied to 10% at 4324567920. Observing reduced mem footprint on canary nodes.
meera: CS note drafted: "We observed GPU OOMs impacting streaming requests for several customers. Mitigation: we temporarily enforced a 512 token cap on streaming requests and quarantined offending API keys. We're scaling cluster and will follow up with root cause analysis." want to send to acme now?
cs-liaison: yes send to acme and quickscribe now. include ETA for full resolution ~15-25m.
sara: performed API key quarantine: `redctl keys suspend ak_live_17 --reason 'runaway generation causing OOMs'` — suspended at 4324567940. Dropped 70% of error tail immediately.
incidents-bot: update: memory pressure decreasing, OOM events on decode-rt-38/39 trending down. Autoscaler added nodes.
kevin: joining now. summary for handoff: - root cause suspected runaway generation from ak_live_17 + no server cap on legacy streaming routes - mitigations done: key suspended, streaming max_tokens override canary -> 10% -> rolling to 100% pending checks, scale-up + draining of worst node - customer comms drafted and sent to impacted customers - monitoring: watch OOM count, container restarts, request drop rate, and per-key request volumes.
sara: handoff notes for next oncall (kevin): 1) confirm canary -> 100% roll (run `redctl config get runtime.streaming.max_tokens_override` then `redctl config rollout --region=us-west-2 --to=100`), 2) keep decode-rt-39 drained for logs and heap dump, 3) coordinate with infra to collect `cuda` logs and coredump if container crashes again (collection path: /var/log/redwood/cuda/), 4) follow up with engineering to add a hard server-side max_tokens enforcement and reject requests > 2048 with 400.
kevin: acknowledged. i'll take 2-hour watch and will escalate to eng-runtime if OOMs reappear after config roll.
meera: one action item for postmortem: add telemetry that correlates per-key token emission rate with GPU memory growth. we currently have per-request token counts but not continuous token-rate.
sara: agree. adding to incident timeline. also collecting heap snapshots from decode-rt-38/39 now. logs attached in incident tracker.
cs-liaison: customers confirmed partial recovery, acme updated: "Thanks, things look better but we'll want RCA." they asked for timeline when permanent fix to server cap will land.
kevin: i'll own follow-up RCA and timeline. will set a draft plan by EOD. handing off this thread to kevin. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: @kevin acknowledged the incident handoff.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT status: mitigated (memory pressure reduced, key suspended, configs rolling). severity downgraded to medium. root cause under investigation.
kevin: marking as oncall-owned. will post updates in this thread. if anything spikes ping me directly.
meera: thanks all — nice rapid coordination.
sara: closing immediate pager. keeping channel open for follow-ups.
